entries.justification: The module is a cohesive owner for the frozen Admin route surface and its shared authorization, validation, and response-envelope rules; splitting those routes without an independently filed boundary design would increase security-policy drift, so this baseline remains reviewable under the growth ratchet.

Authentication, session, invitation, verification, reset, and conversion invariants currently share one security-sensitive state machine; a future split needs its own contract and threat-model ticket rather than a mechanical move, while the twenty-percent ratchet prevents silent continued growth.

Recovery verification, evidence classification, and guarded repair orchestration form one fail-closed operator boundary whose sequencing is more important than file size alone; retain the cohesive owner until a dedicated recovery-package design preserves every forensic and rollback invariant.

This standalone audit intentionally keeps discovery, classification, evidence rendering, and its deterministic safety model together so one operator command owns the complete decision; splitting it is deferred until a separate ticket can preserve its one-command fail-closed evidence contract.

This Browser owner keeps the complete auth-and-lobby affinity family atomic for shard safety; issue #722 owns the follow-up decomposition into smaller affinity-safe groups, so the file stays registered until that work proves unchanged case inventory and producer-consumer ownership.

This Browser owner preserves the complete Bingo, shared-shell, and Admin producer-consumer affinity family as one shard unit; issue #722 owns safe decomposition, and the register prevents further material growth before that case-inventory and affinity proof lands.

This Browser owner keeps the complete Roulette, Slots, and Keno affinity family together so setup and settlement consumers cannot land on different shards; issue #722 owns its affinity-safe decomposition and must preserve exact sorted Browser case identities.

The suite is the single source for deployment-workflow, pull-poller, release, residue, and fail-closed qualification assertions; its scenarios share exact workflow literals and operator boundaries, so a later split requires a dedicated inventory-preserving test-ownership ticket.

The sustained concurrent Browser harness intentionally owns one coordinated server, worker, telemetry, and teardown lifecycle whose failures must be interpreted together; keep it cohesive until a separate harness decomposition can prove identical concurrency and cleanup evidence.

The suite is a single fault-matrix for JSON game-action claims, receipts, journals, epochs, reset rollback, and crash recovery; keeping schedules adjacent makes cross-window omissions visible, while any future split must preserve the named lifecycle matrix and restart coverage.

The disposable MySQL harness owns one privilege-bounded migration, provider, reset, locking, and cleanup lifecycle against a single temporary target; retaining one owner prevents partial cleanup and grant evidence from drifting across independently invoked integration files.

Issue #727 deliberately reduced tests/run_tests.py to a compatibility shim and moved unified discovery, listener, reset, execution, reporting, and teardown lifecycle here; those shared mutable seams remain one orchestrator pending a separately designed runner-package split with exact CLI and case inventories.

The suite provides the broad provider-contract and storage-failure matrix used to compare JSON and connector-free MySQL behavior; its shared fixtures and mutation assertions remain cohesive until a dedicated provider-area test split can preserve every parity seam.

The large-UI stress harness owns one deterministic catalog, render, navigation, and resource-budget scenario whose measurements are meaningful only as a complete run; retain it as one bounded acceptance owner until a dedicated fixture-generator design proves byte-equivalent inputs.

These unit fixtures mirror the complete concurrent Browser harness safety envelope, including worker coordination, timeouts, telemetry, and cleanup; keeping the oracle together avoids mismatched fixture assumptions until the production harness itself receives a governed split.

The suite is the cohesive exact-source oracle for payload, linked-asset, frontend, archive, and index budgets; shared synthetic Git objects and closure assertions make a mechanical split risk divergent fixture semantics, so growth is ratcheted pending a dedicated design.

The benchmark oracle keeps JSON and MySQL request grids, statistical acceptance, governance bindings, and fixture construction in one deterministic model; separating it without a dedicated plan could make provider evidence incomparable, so the review ratchet bounds interim growth.

Roulette currently owns one tightly coupled table, bet-map, motion, result, chip, accessibility, and settlement presentation lifecycle; issue #718 is the governed incremental frontend-lifecycle path, and a direct split before its shared seams land would increase cross-module game risk.
